mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS declines, with t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 7.5% over a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which triggers a shift toward risk-off sentiment and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, or the signal fails to generate a negative return direction with t-test p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production below 99.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in real output, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below 99.0, with t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL above 232.5 over a 3-month window signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to delay rate cuts and increasing real rates, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 232.5, with t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals strong aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payrolls above 200k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals a tight labor market that may force the Fed to maintain high rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds 200k and UNRATE is below 7.8, with t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.0% annualized over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which triggers risk-off behavior and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 is below 1.0%, with t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
